# Behavioral Specification: Life-Cycle TL-UL Gate

## 1. Purpose

This module is a security gate placed between a TL-UL host and a TL-UL device. It conditionally allows bus traffic to pass based on a life-cycle control input. When the life-cycle control does not enable the gate, the module blocks all traffic to the device and returns TL-UL error responses to the host so that the host does not hang.

## 2. General Behavior

The module must operate in one of two broad functional states:

- **Forwarding state**: the module passes TL-UL traffic between the host and the device.
- **Erroring/blocking state**: the module does not forward traffic to the device and instead returns error responses for host requests.

The module must be fail-safe: if the life-cycle enable is not validly asserted, access to the device must be denied.

## 3. Life-Cycle Enable Interpretation

- The life-cycle enable input uses a multi-bit encoding.
- Only the defined ON value is considered enabling.
- All other values, including the OFF value and invalid encodings, must be treated as non-enabling.
- The enable signal is quasi-static and must be synchronized before being applied to the module.

## 4. Reset Behavior

- On reset, the module must enter the erroring/blocking state.
- After reset, no request may be forwarded to the device.
- Any host request presented while the module is in this reset-default state must receive an error response.
- The module may leave this state only after the life-cycle enable is validly ON.

## 5. Forwarding State Requirements

While the module is forwarding:

- All valid host requests must be passed through to the device unchanged.
- All valid device responses must be passed back to the host unchanged.
- The module must not alter the request opcode, address, data, byte enables, size, source identifier, user/security attributes, or any other field.
- The module must not alter the response opcode, data, size, source identifier, sink identifier, error flag, or user/security attributes.
- The module must not reorder, merge, or drop transactions.
- The module must not generate its own error responses in this state.
- Device-reported errors must pass through to the host normally.

## 6. Disabling Transition Requirements

When the life-cycle enable changes from ON to not-ON:

- The module must stop accepting new requests from the host.
- Any new request that has not already been accepted must not be forwarded to the device.
- Requests that were already accepted and are still in flight must be allowed to complete.
- Responses for those in-flight requests must still be returned to the host.
- Only after all such outstanding transactions have completed may the module enter the full erroring/blocking state.

## 7. Erroring/Blocking State Requirements

While the module is in the erroring/blocking state:

- No host request may be forwarded to the device.
- The device-facing request channel must be idle, with no valid request presented.
- Any valid host request must receive a TL-UL error response.
- Error responses must be generated locally and must not require any participation from the device.
- Any response coming from the device must be suppressed and must not be returned to the host.
- The module must not generate unsolicited responses; an error response may only be produced in response to a request.

The error response must:

- Indicate a bus error.
- Use the response opcode appropriate for the original request:
  - A read request must receive a read-data response with the error flag set.
  - A write request must receive a write-acknowledge response with the error flag set.
- Carry the same source identifier and size as the original request.
- Not expose any device data.

## 8. Re-Enabling Transition Requirements

When the life-cycle enable changes from not-ON to ON:

- The module must not immediately resume forwarding if there are outstanding error responses that have not yet been delivered.
- During this re-enabling drain, the module must not accept new requests.
- Once all pending error responses have been accepted by the host, the module may return to the normal forwarding state.
- If no error responses are outstanding, the module should resume forwarding as soon as internal state allows.

## 9. Illegal Internal State and Error Status

- The module must provide a sideband error status indication.
- Under normal operation, including normal erroring/blocking operation, this status must be deasserted.
- If the module detects an illegal or unrecognized internal state, it must assert this status.
- When this status is asserted, the module must force itself into the erroring/blocking state:
  - no traffic may pass to the device,
  - all host requests must receive error responses,
  - the module must remain blocked until reset.

## 10. Configuration

- The module supports a compile-time parameter that selects the number of gating elements inserted in each direction.
- All gating elements must operate as a single logical gate: they must all be enabled together or all disabled together.
- The externally observable behavior must be independent of the selected number of gating elements.
